Mr. Abdus Salam Mamun, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the Opposite Party 
to show cause as to why the impugned Judgment and decree dated 17.2.1990 passed by the learned District Judge, Cox's bazar, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 9 of 1987 affirming the judgment and decree dated 24.12.1986 passed by the Learned Munsif, Chakaria, Cox's bazar in 
Miscellaneous Case No. 174 of 1983 should not be set aside. 

2. Facts leading to the issuance of this Rule are that the Opposite Party Hasan Ali instituted the other Suit No. 17 of 1977 in the Court of the Munsif, Chakaria, Cox's bazar praying for a decree for permanent injunction in respect of the suit property, described in the schedule to the plaint and the suit was decreed exparte on 4.4.1978. decree signed on 8.4.1978. As soon as the Plaintiff came to know about the exparte decree, filed an application on 17.6.1981 under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for restoration of the suit by setting aside the exparte decree on the grounds stated therein and it was registered as Miscellaneous Case NO. 174 of 1983 which, after hearing, was dismissed on 24.12.1986 vide Judgment and Order No. 52, passed by the Learned Munsif Chakaria, Cox's bazar and against the said judgment and order of dismissal the petitioner has preferred the Miscellaneous Appeal NO. 9 of 1987 and by his judgment and order dated 17.2.1990, the learned District Judge, Cox's bazar has also been pleased to dismiss the Appeal on contest upholding the judgment and order dated 24.12.1986 passed by the learned Munsif Being aggrieved by the said judgment and order, the Petitioner-Appellant has preferred this application under Section 115(1) of the Court of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the instant Rule on the grounds that the learned Appellate Court has erred in law in not holding that the service return of the Process Server was not accompanied by any Affidavit or even verification or a declaration as was required by law and examination of the Process Server was essential and that the learned Appellate Court has committed an error in his decision occasioning failure of justice in not holding that inspite of provisions of Rule I 9A of Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure-, examination of the Process Server in the instant case was mandatory, as the Process Server has simply submitted his report about the service of summons without any verification or declaration and the learned Court has also erred in law in not holding that the summons has not been served upon the Defendant. 

3. Mr. J.B.M. Hasan, the learned Advocate appearing for the Petitioner, by placing his reliance upon the case of Abdul Wahab Gazi Vs. Sheikh Haider Ali and others. reported in 1 BLC(AD) 41 submitted that the learned trial Court without finding that the summons was duly served upon the Defendants passed the exparte decree and that the onus to prove that the summons was duly served upon the Defendants was on the Plaintiff and the onus was not discharged when the Process Server has simply submitted his report about the. service of summons by affixing without any verification or declaration, and not examined whereas, his examination is mandatory under Order V Rule 17, 19 and 19A of the Code of Civil Procedure, when the service is by hanging. The learned Appellate Court has erred in law in not looking into the matter in Appeal which has occasioned failure of justice. 

4. Mr. Rabi Shankar Chakraborty. the learned Advocate, appearing for the: opposite Party, has on the other hand, relied upon the case of Md. Insan Ali Vs Mir Abdus Salam, reported in 40 DI.,11(AD) 193, upon which the learned Appellate Court has also placed his reliance and held that the onus has shifted upon the Defendant to prove that the summons was not duly served, as claimed by the Plaintiffs and it was incumbent upon all the Defendants to depose on oath that summons were not served upon them by the Process Server. Relying upon the principle enunciated in this case, the Learned Advocate supported the decision of the Learned Appellate Court praying for discharge of the Rule. 

5. Perused the application, heard the learned Advocates and considered their submissions. 
On perusal of the record of the Other Suit No.367 of 1977, it appears that notices were issued upon the Defendants asking them to show cause as to why Temporary injunction shall not be granted at the initial stage of the suit and from Order No. 4 dated 10.12.1977 appears that the show cause notices have been returned after service and as such temporary injunction was granted and from the Order No. 8 dated 07.3.1978 it appears that summons on the Defendants have been served and since the Defendants did not turn up the suit was fixed for exparte hearing. 

6. The Summons are available in the records and by his report dated 28.1.1978, the Process Server has stated that he offered summons to the Defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3 together with copy of the plaint but they refused to receive it by putting their thumb impressions and as such, he served the summons by hanging in front of their dwelling houses in presence of the witnesses. He made an endorsement at the bottom that he himself has served the summons. 

7. From the exparte decree dated 4.4.1978 it appears that the learned Munsif has not stated anything about his satisfaction on the service of summons. 

8. In 1983 by Ordinance No. XLVIII changes have been introduced in Rule 19 under  Order V by substituting the Rule I9A relating to service of summons. Rule 17 provides the procedure when the Defendant refuses to accept the service, the service shall be fixed by a copy of the 'summons on the outer door or some conspicuous part of the house in which the Defendant ordinarily resides or carries on business. Under Rule 18 the Servicing Officer shall endorse or sign on the original summons returned stating the time, when, manner in which, the summons have been served and the name and address of the person identifying the persons served and witness of' the delivery or tender of the summons and Rule 19 provides for examination of Serving Officer on oath where the summons returned under rule 17 and has not been verified by the affidavit of the serving officer and the Rule 19A is the exception to the general provisions of the Rule 19 which provides as follows: "19A. A declaration made and subscribed by serving officer shall be received as evidence of the facts as to the service or attempted to service of summons."  

9. In the instant case, the learned Appellate Court found that the Plaintiff-Opposite Party has clearly discharged his onus as the Process Server submitted his report along with a declaration that he served the summons by hanging it on the gate of the Defendants, when the later refused to accept it and thereafter, the plaintiff appeared in the Court and deposed on oath that the summons has duly been served and the Defendants could not prove that they were prevented by sufficient causes from appearing in the suit on the date fixed for hearing and they have also failed to prove suppression of summons as alleged. 

10. In the case of Md. Insan Ali Vs. Mir Abdus Salam, reported in 40 DLR (AD) 193 
their Lordships found as follows: "the learned Sub-ordinate Judge on perusal of  the service return, along with the declaration of the process-server, recorded a finding that he was satisfied that the summons was duly served and on the finding decreed the suit exparte. (Underlining is mine).  

11. But on scrutiny of the exparte decree in the instant proceeding it appears that the 
learned Munsif nowhere recorded his satisfaction that the summons has been served upon the Defendants and the service was satisfactory. Without recording his Satisfaction about service, he has disposed of the suit exparte and as such, the instant suit is distinguishable from the case reported in 40 DLR (AD) 193 and the case law enunciated in the reported case, supports the 
contention of the petitioner that the Learned Munsif has proceeded for exparte disposal of the suit without recording his satisfaction on service of summons and as such the same was illegal. 

12. The language of Rule 19A of the Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure, quoted 
above is categorical that ".... The declaration made and subscribed by the serving officer shall he received as evidence of the facts as to the service or attempted to service of summons' meaning that the learned Judge concerned, in such a case must take into cognizance the service of summons and admit the service or attempted to service into evidence on his expressed satisfaction and otherwise it means that he shall record his satisfaction in his exparte decree about the service of summons. Thus before proceeding for exparte disposal a judge needs to record that the summons have been served upon the Defendants to his satisfaction and only after that he can proceed with the suit for exparte disposal and this pre-condition of satisfaction 
regarding service and admitting it into evidence is, of course, lacking in the instant suit. If considered from the factual aspects of this case it is also not believable that a man would sit idle even knowing that he has been restrained by a court by injunction from entering into a land with which he is involved in a dispute. 

13. In the case Abdul Wahab Gazi Vs. Sheikh Haider Ali, reported in 1 BLC (AD) 41 their lordships have considered the provisions of Rule 17, 19 and 19A of the Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

14. Since the learned Munsif has not recorded his satisfaction about the service of 
summons upon the Defendants and without 44 such recorded satisfaction and admitting it into evidence as required by law, proceeded for exparte disposal of the suit this Rule thus succeeds. 

15. In the result, the Rule is made absolute with costs. 
The impugned Judgment and decree, dated 17.2.1990 passed by the learned District Judge, Cox's bazar, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 9 of 1987 dismissing the Appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 24.12.1986 passed by the Learned Munsif: Chakaria, C'ox's bazar in Miscellaneous Case No. 174 of 1983 is hereby set aside. 

The Other Suit No. 367 of 1977 of the Court the Learned Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Chakaria, Cox's bazar is restored by setting aside the exparte decree passed on 4.4.1978 with cost of Tk. 3.000/- and the learned Assistant Judge is directed to proceed with the hearing of the suit after giving the Defendant a chance for filling their written statements, if any, and dispose of the suit as expeditiously as possible. 

Send down the lower Court's records at once. 

End.

Mr. A. K. Badrul Huq, J: By this application under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Third Party- Petitioner in Title Execution Case No. 5 of 1987 arising out of Title Suit No. 205 of 1985 challenges the propriety of a decision recorded by learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet rejecting an application presented by him under Order 21 Rule 99 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying the proceeding of title execution case whereupon Rule was issued calling upon opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 to show cause as to why order No. 115 dated 23.11.1999 passed by learned Senior Assistant Judge (in-charge), Sadar Court, Sylhet rejecting prayer of petitioner for staying all further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 5 of 1987 till disposal of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 pending in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Sylhet should not be set aside. 

	2. The only question that survives for determination in the Civil Revision Petition is whether the order under challenge in Civil Revision petition calls for any interference in exercise of this court's Civil Revisional Jurisdiction under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

	3. For the purpose of appreciating the said question posed and also for a decision essential facts may be noticed. 

	4. Predecessor of opposite party Nos. I and 2 of this Civil Revision Petition as plaintiff laid a suit being Title Suit No. 205 of 1985 in the Court of Munsif, Sadar, Sylhet for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession with respect to property described in schedule to the plaint. The schedule property will be referred to hereinafter as suit property. The Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh as defendant No. 1 contested the said suit on presentation of a written statement. The said suit was dismissed by the judgment and decree dated 23.9.1986. Plaintiff sought setting aside the above judgment and decree through a medium of appeal being title Appeal No. 246 of 1986 before the learned District Judge, Sylhet. Second Court of learned Subordinate Judge, Sylhet heard the appeal and by judgment and decree dated 16.4.1987 allowed the appeal and reversed the decisions rendered by trial Judge and decreed the suit. Decree-holder plaintiff put the decree into execution in Title Execution Case No. 5 of 1987. 

	5. Defendant No. 1 felt dissatisfied with the judgment and decree recorded by appellate Judge and approached this court in a Civil Revision Petition under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained Rule. Civil Revision Petition had been numbered as Civil Revision No. 3 of 1988 (Sylhet). Rule was subsequently discharged by High Court Division by the judgment and order dated 7.3.1989 and 8.3.1989. Civil petition for leave to Appeal No. 330 of 1989 carried by defendant No. 1 Government was also dismissed by Appellate Division on 12.2.1990. Defendant No. 1 Government took a Review Petition before High Court Division to review the judgment and order recorded in Civil Revision No. 3 of 1988. Said Review Petition stood rejected by High Court Division on 10.1.1991. 

	6. Present petitioner Rotish Chandra Das thereafter instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 in the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Sylhet for declaration of title over suit property and also for a declaration that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 205 of 1985 was not binding him. Petitioner Rotish Chandra by way of an petition presented in Title Execution Case No. 5 of 1987 wanted to stay further proceeding of the said Title Execution case till disposal of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991. Said petition was rejected by Executing Court, by order dated 29.5.1991. Petitioner Rotish felt dissatisfied with the above order dated 29.5.1991 and invoked this Court's Civil Revisional Jurisdiction on laying a petition under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Rule was issued and the Civil Revision Petition had been numbered as Civil Revision No. 2069 of 1991. Rule was subsequently discharged on contest by High Court Division by judgment and order dated 13.8.1991. Civil Miscellaneous Petition No. 75 of 1991 was preferred before the Appellate Division and the said Civil Miscellaneous petition was dismissed for non-prosecution. 

	7. Petitioner Rotish Chandra Das obtained an order of injunction in Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 restraining decree-holder Sudhir Chandra Chandan from taking possession over the suit property. Said order of injunction stood set aside by High Court Division order dated 9.11.1993 in F.M.A. No. 758 of 1991. Decree-holder Sudhir Chandra Chandan died during pendency of Execution Proceeding 2.12.1993 and his heirs present opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed an application in the Court for their substitution. The said prayer was rejected by Executing court by the order dated 6.2.1996. Opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 took a Civil Revision Petition before High Court Division against the said order dated 6.2.1996 refusing to substitute them in Execution proceeding. Rule was issued and the said Civil Revision Petition had been numbered as Civil Revision No. 2423 of 1996. Civil Revision case was allowed by High Court Division by judgment dated 21.8.1999 and application for substitution was allowed. High Court Division in the said judgment and order took the view that the case was a very old one and recorded direction to learned Senior Assistant Judge to dispose of Title Execution case within four months from the date of receipt of the order. 

	8. Petitioner Rotish Chandra Das, thereafter filed an application under the provision of Order 21 Rule 99 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Executing Court for staying Title Execution Case No. 5 of 1987 till the disposal of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991. 

	9. Learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet, the Executing Court by the impugned order dated 23.11.1999 rejected the same. In recording rejection learned Senior Assistant Judge took into account the direction given to him by High Court Division in the matter of disposal of Execution case and, therefore, found no ground to stay proceeding of Title Execution case. 

	Feeling dissatisfied, the petitioner Rotish Chandra Das approached this Court in this present application under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained Rule. 

	Mr. A.K.M. Fail along with Mr. Md. Abdul Malek learned Advocates appeared for the petitioner. Opposite party Nos. I and 2 are represented by Mr. J. N. Deb, with Mr. Md. Ekramul Huq and Ms. Rezina Chowdhury, learned Advocates. 

	10. The only contention pressed into service on behalf of third party petitioner is that the petitioner has been on the suit property for the last 33 years and to secure ends of justice his possession is required to be protected and the proceeding of Execution case is required to be stayed till disposal of his suit being Title Suit No. 35 of 1991.

	11. Repelling the said contention it has been canvassed from the side of Decree-holder opposite parties that proceeding of a Decree Execution case cannot be stayed at the instance of a third party to the decree and grave injustice would be caused to them if proceeding of the Title Execution case remained stayed till disposal of petitioner suit. 

	12. In approaching the controversy it is to be noticed first that the petitioner's application for stay of the proceeding of the Execution case had been filed under the provision of Order 21 Rule 99 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the said application he prayed for staying all further proceeding of Title Execution case till disposal of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991. From the statement and the prayer couched in the application it is evidently clear that provision of law had been misquoted and virtually this petition was under the provision of Order 21 Rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

	13. It appears that the Judgment-Debtor -Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh contested the claim of the Decree-holder-opposite party’s upto the Appellate Division but the attempts could not be crowned with success. Present-petitioner's endeavor to get the proceeding of the Execution case stayed could not be successful upto the Appellate Division previously. It appears that by this application dated 23.11.1999 petitioner attempted to reopen the matter which was decided finally upto the Apex Court. The laying of the application dated 23.11.1999 appeared to me as an effort to vet reopened the controversy which got finality upto the Apex Court. Finality much attach to some stage of the proceeding. The course adopted by petitioner is impermissible in law. No litigant got a right to unlimited drought on Courts time and public money in order to get his affairs settled and resolved in the way of he wishes. Every access to justice must not be misused as a licence to file frivolous petition. 

	14. Rule 29 of Order 21 of Code of Civil Procedure enjoins that where a suit is pending in any court against the holder of a decree of such court on the part of the person against whom the decree was passed, the court may, on such terms as to security or otherwise as it thinks fit, stay execution of the decree until the pending suit is decided. The Executing court got no power to order stay of execution where the suit is against Decree-holder filed by Third Party. Since the petitioner is not a party to the suit and the decree and Execution case he got no legal right or character to maintain any application under Rule 29 of Order 21 of the Code to stay further proceeding of Title Execution case. 

	15. Power under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is a power inherent in the Court by virtue of its duty to do justice between the parties. The section does not confer new powers on court but only to save inherent power to make orders necessary for the ends of justice. Section 151 of the Code is only a legislative recognition of well known doctrine and principle that every court got inherent power to act ex debit justice and to do that real justice for the administration of which alone it exists court acts ex debit justice according to equity justice and good conscience of a cause and in consonance with sound judicial principle and also fundamental laws and judicial procedure. 

	16. The facts and materials placed before me and the cheered carrier of the case does not at all demand the exercise of inherent power of this court in staying further proceeding of Title Execution case pending disposal of a suit laid by a Third party-petitioner.

	17. On perusal of the order under challenge in Civil Revision Petition it appears that learned Senior Assistant Judge as the Executing Court took into consideration positive direction recorded by High Court Division directing learned Judge to dispose of Title Execution case within four months from the date of receipt of the judgment by High Court Division. From the order it is not at all manifested that the same is not well founded on law and suffers from patent illegality and legal infirmity and flagrant error of law. The description exercised by learned Assistant Judge in refusing to stay further proceeding of Title Execution case does not at all appear to have exercised arbitrarily and capriciously and the said discretion appears to be judicious enjoined by Tradition methodized by analogy and disciplined by system. 

	18. No interference is therefore, called for. 

	19. Resultantly, the Rule arising out of Civil Revision Petition stands discharged. 

	20. Order of stay granted at the time of issuance of Rule on 28.11.1999 stands vacated. Title Execution Case No. 5 of 1987 will proceed in accordance with law. 

	21. Regard being had to the facets and circumstances of the case and the blameworthy conduct of the Third party-petitioner, I award a cost of Taka Five Thousand against him.

End.

Mr. Md. Mamtazuddin Ahmed, J: This Rule at the instance of the defendant No. 3 is directed against the judgment and order 18.5.1965 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Rajshahi, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 31 of 1995 affirming the order dated 29.4.1995 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 44 of 1991 by the Assistant Judge, Godagari, rejecting the application under order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

	2. The facts relevant for the purpose of the disposal of the Rule are that opposite parties herein being plaintiffs instituted the suit for cancellation of the document dated 2.3.1991 purported to have executed by late Elahi Box in favour of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 of the suit The defendant No. 3 filed an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the exparte decree dated 3.8.1991 stating inter alia that on 16.9.1991 the petitioner received a postal envelop and opened the same and found a notice form in the envelop fixing on 5.3.1991 for his appearance and for filing written statements in the original suit. The petitioner thereafter engaged Advocate for searching and taking information about the original suit and who informed the petitioner orally that he was the defendant No. 3 of the original suit and also informed him that 1.7.1991 was fixed for his appearance and filing written statement and on that date 20.7.1991 had fixed for exparte hearing the suit. The petitioner further stated that he did not receive any summons or notice before 16.9.1901. The process server did not serve summons upon the petitioner and as a result he could not appear and file written statements and contested the suit as he had no knowledge about the suit earlier than 16.9.1991. And further stated that if the petitioner would know about the suit before 16.9.1991 he would have certainly contested the said suit and also stated that the plaintiff opposite parties in collusion with the process server managed to show false service of summons but in tact the process server did not visit to the house of the petitioner for effecting service of summons of the said suit.

	3. The plaintiff-opposite parties con-tested the Miscellaneous Case by filing written objection denying the statements and allegations made in the miscellaneous case and stated specifically that the case is barred by limitation and the summons of the suit were duly' served upon the defendants including the petitioner. It was also contended that the Criminal Case is pending in the Court of Additional District Magistrate and to avoid conviction the petitioner has taken fraudulent tactics and kept himself away from the Court in spite of service of the summons. 

	4. The learned Assistant Judge after hearing the parties and on consideration of the evidence on record rejected the, application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

	5. Being aggrieved by the said order of rejection passed by the learned Assistant Judge the petitioner preferred appeal before the District Judge, Raishahi, and on transfer the learned Subordinate Judge 2nd Court, Rajshahi, disallowed the appeal and affirmed the order of the Trial Court. 

	6. Mr. Shaheed Alam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-petitioners has taken me to the judgments of both the courts below and other materials on record and submits that the court below failed to take notice that when a summon is returned stating that the process server served the summons affixing the copy under Rule 17, the court shall, if the return under that rule has riot been verified by affidavit of the serving officer, shall examine the serving officer on oath touching the proceedings or make such further inquiry in the matter but the courts below accepted the service without observing by those formalities although the requirements are mandatory in law and in spite of such position the courts below failed to advert to those materials on record arid committed error of law resulting in any error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Mr. Alam next submits that from the face of the summons it would be evident that the Nazir of the Cowl handed over the summons of the suit for service to the process server on 2.3.1991 and on the same date i.e. 2.3.199 I at 10 A. M. (Morning) the process server had shown to have served the summons which definitely indicates that there was a collusion between the process-server and the opposite parties and the return (report) of service is false and fraudulent which has been made so that the opposite parties being plaintiffs can get a walk- over but both the courts failed to notice those aspects of the case and passing the impugned order committed error of law which has occasioned failure of justice. Mr. Alam again submits that the courts below took wrong presumption that the petitioner knew about the suit earlier on the basis of the information ship, but in fact. the information ship was written and filed by the learned Advocate when t he petitioner requested the learned Advocate to ascertain the exact position of the suit and that shows there was non-application of judicial mind and as such on wrong findings passed the impugned order which is liable to be set aside and further submits that the petitioner only on 16.9.1991 came to know about the suit on receipt of the enveloped and he filed the miscellaneous case under order 9 rule 13 C.P.C. on 30.9.1991 but the findings of the cowls below are wrong to the effect that the case is barred by limitation which has occasioned failure of justice. 

	7. Mr. Alam again contends that the provisions of Order 5 Rule 17 speak that 
when the serving officer after using all due and reasonable diligence cannot find the defendant the serving officer shall affix a copy of the summons on the outer door or some other conspicuous part of the house in which the defendant ordinarily resides and shall then return the original to the court from which it was issued with a report endorsed there on stating that he has so affixed the copy, the circumstances under which he did so. and the name and address of the person by whom the house was identified and whose presence the copy was affixed and in the service return of this case the process server gave names of two persons but those persons were not produced to support the identification of the house and affixing of the same and thereby the plaintiff-opposite parties failed to prove the service of summons and the courts below failed to consider those requirement law but rejecting application under Order 9 Rule 13 C.P.0 committed error of law which has occasioned failure of justice. 

	8. Mr. Shaheed Alam to support his submission has referred to the decision in the case of Upendra Chandra Rishi and others Vs. Sufia Begum and others reported in 42 DLR (AD) 285. wherein their Lordships observed summons served by process-server without noting the name and addresses of Mokabila witnesses in the service return, in that case process-server appearing in Court as a witnesses his evidence without examining the Mokabila witnesses is not acceptable. It is obligatory upon the process-serve to mention in his report the name and address of the person if any, by whom the house in question was identified and in whose presence the copy of summons was affixed and when service reports were devoid of these essential information, they were unacceptable mere personal appearance of the process-server as a witness in Court did not made the report acceptable. 

	9. Mr. Alam further submits that the findings of both Court are palpably wrong to the effect the defendants No. 3 has no standi to file application under order 9 rule 13 of the CPC as no decree has been passed against the defendant No. 3 and those findings are not based on proper appreciation of the law in as much as the petitioner No. 1 was made party being defendant No. 3 making some allegations against him in the plaints and in that case defendant No. 3 had/has all the right to defend himself and asking for setting aside the exparte decree which was obtained fraudulently and coming to the contrary findings beyond the scope law both the Courts committed error of law which has occasioned failure of justice. 

	10. He submits further that when the petitioner failed to get remedy, he along with his wives legally moved the High Court. Division and brought. to the notice of the Court as to committing wrong by the courts below upon which, the High Court Division can rectify the error of the courts below which has come to its notice and has referred to the decisions such as (I) in the ease Ashhini Kumar Karmaker and others Vs. Hari Mohan and others reported in 36 DLR (AD) 1 (11). In the case of Ramjil Kumar Rakshit Vs. Sadhin Kumar Choudhury reported in 38 DLR 39 and upon reading of those decisions it appears that under the provision of Section 115 CPC the High Court Division can rectify the error of law in a matter which has come to its notice suo-motu when the impugned order has been Passed by a court subordinate to the High Court Division in which no appeal lies I hereto and urges for making the Rule absolute. 

	11. Mr. A. K. M. Asaduzzaman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff opposite parties submits that the opposite parties plaintiffs did not seek any relief against the defendant No. 3 and the decree was not passed against him. Both the Courts came to the findings that the decree having not been sought against the defendant No. 3 he cannot be said to have prejudiced by the impugned judgment and both the courts concurrently found that he is not entitled to seek any relief and in view of such materials on record, and when both the Courts resolved the facts concurrently as such it calls for no interference by this Court. He further referring to the deposition of the defendant No. 3 who deposed as P.W. 1 in the Miscellaneous case submits that from the cross examination of the P.W. 1 it is found that his wives received the summons and in view of the fact that when his wives received the summons they did not come before the Court for setting aside the decree but the defendant No. 3 in spite of no relief sought against him came before the court but both the courts believed the service of summons and in view of such concurrent findings and decisions this court calls for no interfere in the matter. In support of his contention Mr. Asauddzaman has referred to the decision in the case of Mr. Santosh Chopra Vs. Teja Singh and another reported in A.I.R. 1977 (Delhi)-110 wherein his Lordship came to the conclusion that:- 

	“On the very reading of the Rule it is clear that it is only the defendant in an action who can move an application under this provision of law. A person who is not a party, though he may he interested in the suit, is not entitled to apply under this Rule. In deed, even a person who is formally a party but against whom nothing is said in the operative portion of the decree or who has been expressly exempted from a decree cannot apply under this Rule to set aside an exparte decree." 

	Another decision in the case of Lala Ajodhya Prasad Vs. Mosammat Katori reported in 1.C. 1921-484 wherein his Lordships held that the court has no jurisdiction to set aside an exparte decree and order when the whole case to be re-opened at the instance of a person not in any way interested in the decision of the case and who has been expressly exempted from the decree. Learned Advocate has referred to another decision in the ease of Yelavarti Anasuyamma Vs. Chennupati Raghavamma reported in A. I. R 1978- (Andhra)-406 wherein his Lordship observed as follows:-

	"No court shall set aside a decree passed exparte merely on the ground that I here has been an irregularity in the service of summons if it is satisfied that the defendant had notice of the date of hearing and had sufficient time to appear and answer the plaintiff's claim." 

	12. Learned Advocate further con-tends that from the records it would be evident that the plaintiffs acted fairly and did not resort to any fraudulent activities but both the Courts found concurrently that the summons were served upon the defendants and having refused to entertain the application under Order 9 Rule 13 CPC concurrently this Court needs not interfere in such matter where the courts committed no error of law. 

	13. Now in view of the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners that the summons were not served and in order to resolve this point the order by which the summons shown to have served is required to be considered and for proper appreciation of the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner the relevant orders may be reproduced from the 
original order sheets order Nos. 4,5 and 6 read as follows:-

	৪ বাদী উপস্থিত। সমন ও A/D ফেরত আসে নাই। আগামী তাং ১৫/৫/৯১ তাং S/R স্বাক্ষরঃ-
সিনিয়র সহকারী জজ
গোদাগাড়ী উপজেলা,
রাজশাহী।

S/R
স্বাক্ষরঃ-
	৬ বাদী হাজিরা দিয়াছে। ১-৩ নং সমন জারী অস্তে ফেরত আসিয়াছে। বিবাদী জবাব দাখিল করে নাই। আগামী তাং ২০/৭/৯১তাং এক তরফা।

	14. From the order No. 6 it appears that on the date the court without considering the nature of service of summons and without examining the process server in view of the service of summons under Rule 17 without complying the provision of Rule 19 abruptly fixed the case for cxparte hearing on 20.7.1991 on further scrutiny of the record it does not reflect that the learned Assistant Judge considered the manner of service of the summons but abruptly fixed on 20.7.1991 for exparte disposal in view of such service the Assistant Judge erred in law in fixing the case for exparte hearing by the same order upon scrutiny of the original service return it appears that the summons were served affixing a copy of the summons on the outer door of the defendants as identified by the two witnesses namely Nazrul Islam and Abu Bakar on 2.3.1991 at 10 A M, the same date of receipt of the summons from the office. It may be noted that seal bearing in the service return has been interpolated and tried to make 1.3.1991 instead of' 2.3.1991. At the hearing of the miscellaneous case process server deposed as P.W. 2 and stated that he received the summons on 1.3.1991 from office and served the same on 2.3.1991 and proved the summons as exhibit K. It was a ease of service by affixing of copy of the summons as the petitioners (defendants) refused to receive the summons exhibit "A" and on close scrutiny of the exhibit "A" it is found to be not satisfactory which has already been indicated that the date of receipt of the summons by the process server appears to have interpolated and tried to make 1.3.1991 from 2.:3.1991. 

	Rule 69 of the Civil Rules and orders provides that:-

	“Service should always be personal wherever practicable (order. 12) and the Courts ought riot in exparte cases to act upon anything short of personal service until they are satisfied that personal service could not reasonably be effected." 

	On thorough examination of the judgments of both the Courts it has been found that the courts below did not consider those aspects of the case. Exhibit A gained acceptance by the Court though none of the witness’s presence or allegedly identified home of the defendants and whose presence delivered or tendered of the summons which is wrong. It further appears from the summons that the process server did not verify the service return by affidavit as requires by order 5 rule 19 of the CPC. 

	14(a). On perusal of the materials before this court and submission of the Learned Advocate for the petitioners it has been noticed that both the courts failed to consider main aspect of the case. It appears that the Courts below tried to shift the onus upon the petitioner to prove service or the summons but in fact when the petitioner came up with the allegations t hat the summons were not served in that case the OTILIS lies upon the persons who support ed and claimed the benefit under the expurte decree and have to show that the summons were legally served. But both the courts misdirected themselves in findings that the onus lies upon the petitioner. The Rule of Evidence is that where the initial onus is discharged by the plaintiffs by giving a slightest evidence the burden shifts to the defendant to prove the contrary. My view has received sup-port in the case of Amirun Nessa and others Vs. Golam Kashem and others reported in 42 DLR-499. But in this case it has been found that only process server came to depose but none of the witnesses as mentioned in the service return was not produced to prove the service of the summons. 

	15. From the order dated 1.7.1991 it appears that the learned Assistant Judge failed to consider the manner of service and having not specifically mentioned as to acceptance of the service or nature of the service and fixed for exparte disposal of the suit and that aspect also was not considered by the Appellate Court and committed error of law. This view of mine finds support in the case of S.K. Haider Ali Vs. Abdul Wahab Gazi and others reported in 49 DLR -251. 

	16. I have already indicated that the alleged service of summons cannot be taken to be service within the scope of the order 5 rules 16.17,18 and 19 of CPC and having regard to the decision of the Appellate Division reported in 42 DLR (AD) 285 referred to above by the petitioners I find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners. The points as have been raised by the learned Advocate for the opposite party that the decree was not sought against the defendant No. 3 and also decree was not passed against him and in that view of the matter the defendant No. 3 has no locus standi to the Miscellaneous case, I have perused the plaint where from it appears that several allegations made against the defendant No. 3 and also made him defendant. No. 3 to the suit though the decree was not sought but the allegations are there ICI in that case defendant No. 3 has right t o defend himself and he has locus standi to seek for setting aside the exparte decree in as much as the principle that no man should be condemned unheard is applicable to judicial proceedings and to that contention a reference may be made in the ease of Abul Hossain Akand (AD) and others Vs. Abul Kalam Azad and another reported in 49 DI.,R (AD) 257. However ultimately all the defendants preferred this revisional application before this court and sought for setting aside the exparte decree and this court issued the Rule, Whenever any wrong or error committed by any court Subordinate of High Court Division can rectify any error of law committed by the courts below and even suo-motu. 

	17. Before parting with the case, I feel it pertinent to observe that a "decree" should be understood a contested "decree" but not an exparte "decree" which always remains a questionable decree. The celebrated jurists had time and again pronounced that the Judges should be leaned to allow the defaulting party to put their grievance or cause before the court and the issue thereof should always be resolved on contested hearing. I find in this case the exparte decree was given within 33 clays and the defendants came before the court within about two months from the date of exparte decree. But both the courts maintained the exparte decree without allowing the other side to put their grievance though they came within the v very short time. But the learned judges allowed the dispute to continue for ast more than 8 years which could easily be resolved upon contested hearing and a proper decree could be pronounced by the 
court which can be termed a "decree" and not a "exparte decree" or questionable decree. 

	18. In view of my above discussions and the reasons stated above I find sub-stance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners I find both the Courts committed error of law in accepting the service of summons without considering the manner of service resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice which calls interference by this court. 

	19. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The application under Order 9 Rule 13 CPC is allowed and thereby the original suit restored to its original file and number. It appears that the suit is pending since 1991 and in that view of the matter the learned Assistant Judge is directed to dispose of the suit strictly within 6 (six) months from the date of receipts of this judgment and order. 

20. Send clown the records at once.

End.

Mr. Mohammad Fazlul Karim, J.:- The petitioners seek leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 12.06.2004 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.4525 of 2001 discharging the rule and affirming those dated 19.08.2001 passed by Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chandpur in Money Execution Case No.8 of 2001 (arising out of Title Suit No.1 of 1998) rejecting the application for stay of the execution proceeding:

<u>2. Sonali Bank the respondent No.2 as the plaintiff' instituted Title Suit No. 1 of 1998 for realization of Tk. 9,42,866.21 impleading the present defendant. The suit was decreed on contest. Thereafter the bank put the decree into execution being Title Execution Case No.8 of 2000. In the execution proceeding the present-petitioner, the judgment-debtor, filed an application for stay of the execution proceeding under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the ground that the judgment-debtor had also obtained a decree against the respondent No.2 Bank for an amount of Tk.15,45,002/-. The Artha Rin Adalat after hearing the decree holder and judgment-debtor rejected the application by impugned order dated 19.08.2001.</u>

3. Mr. Md. Harunur Rashid, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submitted that the High Court Division ought to have found that the petitioner obtained decree in Money Suit No.1 of 1997 against respondent No.2-Bank for Tk.15,45,002/- which is under challenge and respondent No.2-Bank obtained decree in Title Suit No.1 of 1998 against the petitioners for Tk. 9,42,866.21 paisa which is not under challenge due to subsection 2 of section 7 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 and if Bank succeeds in appeal there is no bar to realize the decreetal amount and until disposal of the appeal the respondent No.2 Bank can not start the execution proceeding and put in auction the property for sale and the impugned judgment and order offends against the guarantee of right to property given by the Constitution The learned Advocate further submitted that the High Court Division committed serious error of law in discharging the rule ignoring the fact that the decree of civil court in both the suits are binding upon the parties and the High Court Division ought to have given a direction to the respondent No.2 to the effect that let the appeal be disposed of within two months meanwhile execution proceeding may be stayed.

<u>4. The High Court Division held that:</u>

<u>"The respondent bank obtained the decree from the jurisdiction of the Artha Rin Adalat and the judgment debtor the present petitioner obtained the decree against the bank from ordinary civil court and that decree is now the subject matter of appeal pending before this court, pendency of the appeal cannot be the ground for stay of the execution proceeding pending in the court of Artha Rin Adalat. From the impugned order does not seem to was that the Artha Rin Adalat passed the order without having jurisdiction or that the Adalat acted in excess of its jurisdiction. The writ petition is otherwise also not maintainable."</u>

<u>5. It is true that the petitioners obtained a decree against the present plaintiff for Tk.15,45,002/- which is more than the amount claimed by the present respondent in its suit but the above decree is under-challenge. In the instant case, only an appeal under section 7(2) could be preferred' challenging the decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and in the absence of any such appeal, we do not find that the petitioner's application for stay of the Artha Rin Execution Case No.2 of 2001 is maintainable. If in the petitioners suit the decree is maintained finally the petitioner can get the decree executed in accordance with law but under the provision of Artha Rin Adalat the proceeding in the execution case can not be stayed.</u>

6. This petition is, accordingly, dismissed.

End.
